item.title: Version 1.0.0
item.description:
Read this first: you have to reset the permission once

macOS ties your Accessibility grant to the app's code signature. Every release up to 0.3.1 was signed with a hash of the build itself, so it changed with every version. 1.0.0 uses a stable certificate, so this stops here, but your Mac still has the old rule stored, and after this update GhostType will be denied while System Settings still shows the switch as on.

Toggling the switch will not fix it. Removing GhostType from the list will not fix it. Run this in Terminal, then relaunch GhostType and approve it when asked:

sudo tccutil reset Accessibility com.ghosttype.app
sudo tccutil reset ListenEvent com.ghosttype.app
sudo killall tccd

Once is enough.

What's new

GhostType now runs on its own. It ships with llama.cpp and downloads a model on first run, so it no longer needs LM Studio or Ollama. If you already run a server, it still points at that instead.

  • Bundled llama.cpp backend, with a model catalogue from 0.5 GB to 2.7 GB
  • Real fill-in-the-middle: the text after your cursor is used, so suggestions join what you already typed
  • Grammar-constrained generation, so a one-line suggestion stays one line
  • Learns from the completions you accept, locally
  • Stays quiet in password fields, credential apps, and sign-in pages
  • Tab accepts one word at a time, and works in Japanese and Chinese
  • Relicensed to MIT
